In addition: Warning message:
In RGEOSBinTopoFunc(spgeom1, spgeom2, byid, id, drop_lower_td, "rgeos_intersection") :

Does anyone know how to fix this error?

Best regards,

Marie

messages.author: 1c354fcf0a5dab6b
messages.subject: Re: Error message in barrier models
parts:
Hi,

I think that I finally figured out what was the problem.
Actually, even after updating the packages, the problem still persisted. However, after looking to your figure, its resolution was much better than mine. Thus, I thought that the problem could be due the resolution of the polygon.
Knowing that the argument ''worldHires'' in the map() function provides maps with higher resolution than the ''world'' argument, I tryed to draw the polygon according this specific argument. Although my figure still looks different than yours (see attaced file), the code finally works. Despite of this, I had to improve your code a little bit and maybe you want to update it for the next time. Here are the codelines that I used:


data("worldHiresMapEnv")

nor_coast_poly <- map("worldHires", "norway", fill=TRUE, col="transparent",
                      plot=FALSE, ylim=c(58,72))
nor_coast_poly$names
IDs <- sapply(strsplit(nor_coast_poly$names, ":"), function(x) x[1])
nor_coast_poly_sp <- map2SpatialPolygons(nor_coast_poly, IDs=IDs,
                                         proj4string=CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84"))
# - copy-paste ended

## We are interested here in a small part of the Norwegian coast
# - it is important not to use a polygon for the whole Norwegian cost
# - limit the polygon to where you have data
# - this is to keep the mesh small
# - a too large mesh leads to a very slow algorithm!

loc3 = matrix(c(4,60.6, 8,60.6, 4,61.5, 8,61.5), 4, 2, byrow = T)
# - this is set to give the right extent of the mesh
# - you can use data locations instead
# - a bit extra offset will be added by the mesh function

square = bakka.square.polygon(xlim=range(loc3[ ,1]), ylim=range(loc3[ ,2]), ret.SP = T)
# - This is the study area
# - Assumption: you are interested in fitting and/or predicting locations inside here
# - You only care about the water area, since land is a barrier

square@proj4string=nor_coast_poly_sp@proj4string

poly3 = gIntersection(nor_coast_poly_sp, square)


Thank you very much for your help!

Best regards,

Marie

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Error message in barrier models
parts:
Hi both,
I think my earlier reply went just to the group mail so you may have missed it.
Yes, the problem was definitely the resolution, since your "coastline" was self-intersecting.

I'm thinking of ways to more easily detect and provide general workarounds for these issues, since a lot of GIS data are geographically impossible in this way, and there is no "one true way" to interpret such geographically impossible input data.  Higher resolution solves part of the problem, but one often wants to do a _safe_ coarsening to avoid creating too many triangles than necessary, etc.  but since this is a computational geometry problem, there aren't that many statisticians working on it...

Finn

Hi Finn,

Thank you for your comments. Defintely, I didn't see your former comment.
I think that a too high coastline resoultion really could be a problem when defining a mesh. Once I was defining my mesh based on a high resolution shapefile and it revealed to be hard to set a good mesh within more narrow spaces. Thus, at the end I decided to use a coarser shapefile which, at that time, resolved my main problem.
However, I think that using higher resolution shapefiles really could improve some important analysis, specifically those related to coastal environments, which usually have a lot of inlets. It would be great if in the near future some statistician may resolve this computational geometry problem....

Best regards,

Marie

Finn
